correctness.rationale: Carlisle–Henson Theorem 11.4 states that an n-type is principal exactly when all coordinates lie along one piecewise segment with distinguished point p as endpoint after permutation. For a principal tuple the ordered radial distances t_i=d(p,a_i) determine d(a_i,a_j)=|t_i-t_j| and the finite-tree pseudometric; quantifier elimination thus identifies a unique principal q_t for each t in [0,r]^n. For any realizations of q_t and q_s, triangle inequality bounds max_i d(a_i,b_i) below by max_i|t_i-s_i|; both can be placed on a single geodesic ray, meeting that bound and proving the exact sup-metric cube. Carlisle–Henson Lemma 8.7 identifies S_1 with [0,r] and Proposition 8.8 gives dens S_2=continuum; repeating a coordinate is an isometric embedding into S_n for n>=2, while finite real pseudometrics bound |S_n| by continuum. The compact principal cube is separable/closed, so nonprincipal complement retains continuum density from n=2 onward. Exact rational-grid finite identity checks in inspected verify.py are corroborative, not model-theoretic proof.
